hook: SCP-7179 opens like a gentle answer to what happens after death, but its real subject is time. It is short and built almost entirely from one observation log, so give its final stretch your full attention. Content note: the later entries include graphic violence against others and repeated self-destruction, stated plainly.
whyItMatters: It belongs to a lettered anthology (the page links to neighbors such as D is for Dermatology), and its subtitle, E is for Eternity, names the true subject before you begin. The afterlife it describes is not a punishment but a private paradise, and the piece asks what paradise means when it never ends. It needs no monster and no breach, only a timestamp column and a lot of empty space.
thingsToNotice:
Paul Hiddleston, a terminally ill man secretly fitted with a soul-tracking construct, arrives on his island to three compliant women, drug-like fruit and endless sun, and the log follows him for far longer than any human scale. Food, cooking, farming and then centuries of building each buy him a stretch of purpose before running dry, and the gaps between entries widen as they do.

The turn is brutal and plain: around year 11,902 he tears the three women apart, later experiments on their reassembled bodies, and then turns on himself, crushing his body under tons of stone and burning himself to ash, each time healing and growing more numb. By a trillion years he simply stops moving.

The long columns of ellipses make you scroll through dead time, and the last entry says that only one second of eternity has passed, which reframes everything above it as nothing. A footnote adds that data can flow out but never in, so the observers can watch and never help.
